events.title: Equans - CV Services Group
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Equans SAS (Equans) proposed to acquire 80% of the share capital
of CV Services Group Pty Ltd (CV Services Group) either directly or
through a wholly-owned subsidiary (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Equans, is a global energy and technical services
company headquartered in France. In Australia, Equans operates
through a local subsidiary, which supplies:
• electrical and communications installation;
• facility management services, including;
o installation and maintenance of heating, ventilation
and air conditioning (HVAC); and
o fire protection products; and
• audio-visual integration and digital signage.
The target, CV Services Group, is an Australian technical services
company. It supplies:
• infrastructure services;
• electrical design, installation and construction;
• facility management services; and
• media and signage manufacturing and installation.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The parties overlap in the supply of:
• electrical construction services;
• facility management services; and
• signage solutions.
The parties also have a limited vertical relationship in the supply of
signage solutions for electrical construction services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Equans and CV Services Group do not appear to compete closely
in the supply of electrical construction services, facility
management services, or signage solutions in Australia.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity will continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details:
Vector JV Bidco, Inc, a special purpose vehicle controlled by Oaktree
Capital Holdings, LLC (Oaktree), applied for a notification waiver in
respect of its proposed:
▪ acquisition of 100% of the share capital in in each of VXMT
Corporation, Vivax (Asia) Ltd, Metrotech Vertriebs GmbH,
Vivax Metrotech Sdn. Bhd., Vivax-Metrotech Ltd. and Vivax-
Metrotech SAS (together, Vivax); and
▪ grant to AMI Holding GmbH, the vendor, of a 40% indirect
equity participation in Vector JV Bidco through the vendor’s
investment in Vector JV Topco, Inc,
as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
6 July 2026

Oaktree is indirectly jointly controlled by Oaktree Capital Group
Holdings GP, LLC; and Brookfield Corporation (together with its
subsidiaries, Brookfield Group).
Oaktree is a global investment manager headquartered in Los
Angeles, USA, specialising in alternative investments. Oaktree
pursues an opportunistic, value-oriented and risk-controlled
approach to investments in distressed debt, high yield bonds,
convertible securities, senior loans, corporate control, real estate,
emerging market equities and mezzanine finance. Oaktree has
investments in a range of companies in Australia including IT
businesses and health and wellness food manufacturing, among
others.
Brookfield Group is a global investment firm that deploys pools of
discretionary capital for investors across its core businesses,
including its asset management business and its operating
businesses focused on renewable power and transition,
infrastructure, private equity, and real estate. Brookfield Group is a
public company, co-listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the
Toronto Stock Exchange. Brookfield Group has investments in
Australia across a range of sectors, including infrastructure and
energy. Brookfield Group is in the process of acquiring the remaining
interest in Oaktree.
Vivax is a global surveying instrument manufacturer. Its products are
used for locating and mapping buried utilities and inspecting the
interior of pipes and ducts. In Australia, Vivax predominantly supplies
precision pipes and cable locating equipment and related
accessories through an independent third-party distributor. Vivax
also provide full calibration of their pipe and cable locaters in
Australia.
AMI Holding GmbH is the current Germany-based holding company
for Vivax.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there are no material competitive overlaps between Oaktree,
Brookfield Group and Vivax in the supply of utility services,
and surveying instruments, particularly underground utility
detection equipment in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of surveying instruments,
including underground utility detection equipment in
Australia.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
Siemens Energy Limited (together with its corporate group, Siemens
Energy) applied for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed
acquisition of the entire issued share capital of Camlin Limited and
its global subsidiaries (Camlin Group), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
6 July 2026

The acquirer, Siemens Energy, is headquartered in Germany and
operates in four main business areas: (i) gas services; (ii) grid
technologies; (iii) transformation of industry; and (iv) Siemens
Gamesa Renewable Energy. Siemens Energy is active in the energy
sector, offering products and services in conventional and renewable
power technologies, grid technology, energy storage and solutions
for electrifying industrial processes. Siemens Energy has over
100,000 employees across 90 countries.
The target, Camlin Group, is a private company, headquartered in
Northern Ireland, which provides monitoring solutions for the energy
sector and railways. Camlin Group provides services in over 45
countries from its offices in the UK, the US, France and China, and its
21 facilities in 17 countries. Camlin Group has around 600
employees globally. In Australia, Camlin Group is active through
Camlin (Australia) Pty Ltd, the primary vehicle with which to contract
with Australian customers. Globally, Camlin Group operates in two
business areas:
• Energy – Camlin Group provides solutions for real-time
monitoring and predictive fault management across the
power chain (i.e., generation, transmission, distribution and
private networks). In particular, Camlin Group provides its
sensing technology and intelligent analytics solutions for: (i)
low voltage networks, (ii) overhead lines, (iii) transformer
monitoring, (iv) switchgear/circuit breaker monitoring, (v)
generator monitoring, and (vi) inbuilding power networks.
These solutions account for the vast majority their business.
• Rail – Camlin Group provides visual in-service, non-intrusive
inspection solutions of pantographs, catenary, roofs, bogies
and signalling power for fleet and infrastructure operators to
detect issues early. However, these solutions only account
for a small proportion of Camlin Group’s business.
Globally, the parties both supply of monitoring solutions for (i)
transformers, (ii) switchgears/circuit breakers and (iii) overhead
lines. However, the application states that Siemens Energy does not
supply any of these monitoring solutions in Australia. Further, Camlin
Group does not supply any monitoring solutions for overhead lines in
Australia.
Globally, Siemens Energy also supplies transformers and
switchgears/circuit breakers.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Siemens Energy and
Camlin Group in the supply of monitoring solutions for
transformers and switchgears/circuit breakers in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of monitoring solutions for
transformers and switchgears/circuit breakers for
customers in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects in Australia resulting from exclusionary conduct
post-acquisition.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

products using both direct and indirect channels. It has no direct

The target, Complete Plaster, is a plasterboard supply business
located in Port Macquarie. It distributes plasterboard, fibre cement,
accessories, and tools in the Port Macquarie region and surrounding

entirely manufactured by CSR, with only tools being third party

fibre cement in Port Macquarie and surrounding areas.

• There is no horizontal overlap between CSR and Complete
Plaster.
• CSR would be unlikely to have the ability or incentive to foreclose

across application management, cognitive infrastructure,
cybersecurity, data and analytics, enterprise applications, business

recruitment services industry. The target is Randstad’s technology

technology solutions and IT consulting services in Europe and

determination_table_content.details:
Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA (Bertelsmann) proposes to merge its
music publishing and recording business, Bertelsmann Music Group
(BMG), with the music publishing and recording business operated
under the Concord label and trademark (Concord), which is currently
majority owned and controlled by Axton Holdings, LLC (Axton).
The proposed merger transaction would involve Bertelsmann and
Axton incorporating a new holding company (New MusicCo), to
which both Bertelsmann – via subsidiaries comprising BMG – and
Axton via Concord will contribute their respective music recording
and publishing businesses (the Acquisition). Post-transaction, New
MusicCo would be majority owned and controlled by Bertelsmann.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Bertelsmann is a German multinational media, services and
education group operating across a number of industries. BMG is
the music publishing and music recording division of Bertelsmann.
In Australia, BMG acquires rights from songwriters and composers
and supplies music publishing services and recorded music
products.
Concord is an independent, US-based music publishing and
recording company supporting artists globally. In Australia, Concord
supplies music publishing services and recorded music products.

The Parties overlap in the supply of music recording and music
publishing services.
Bertelsmann’s media arm has an interest in Freemantle Australia
and Eureka Productions, an acquirer of synchronisation rights. BMG
and Concord both license their music publishing rights for
synchronisation usage in Australia to advertisers, broadcasters, and
film and TV production companies.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in

alternative suppliers of music recording and music publishing
services in Australia and globally. These competitors include

numerous small-to-medium suppliers of music recording and
music publishing services.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival music publishers’ access to sub-
publishing services because there are sufficient alternative
suppliers of such services.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival music publishers’ access to sales
channels for their synchronisation rights or to foreclose rival TV
and film producers’ access to synchronisation rights because
there are sufficient alternative suppliers and sufficient
alternative acquirers of synchronisation rights.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia
items: The various ways and extent to which competition takes place in the supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia (including price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, customer service, claims handling and renewals).

The extent to which IAG and RACI compete closely in Western Australia, including in relation to price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, customer service, claims handling and renewals.

The competitive significance of RACI in Western Australia, and the likely future competitiveness of RACI absent the Acquisition (taking into account RACI’s position as a state-based organisation, capital adequacy requirements, and RACI’s ability to raise capital).
The competitive constraint from rival insurers on IAG post-Acquisition in Western Australia.
The likelihood, timeliness and sufficiency of new entry into or expansion of the supply of home and contents insurance in Western Australia, including the possible impediments to this.
The impact of the use of different brands (both underwriter and third-party brands) on competition for consumers.
How regulatory costs, claims cost volatility, reinsurance costs and geographic diversity impact RACI’s ability to supply home and contents insurance.
The extent to which RACI’s motor insurance portfolio could mitigate against loss events in RACI’s home and contents insurance portfolio.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Competitive effects in the retail supply of motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia
items: The various ways and extent to which competition takes place in the supply motor vehicle insurance in Western Australia (including price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, service quality, claims handling and renewals).

The extent to which IAG and RACI compete closely in Western Australia including in relation to price, coverage and other terms of the insurance product offering, customer service, claims handling and renewals.

The competitive significance of RACI in Western Australia, and the likely future competitiveness of RACI absent the Acquisition (taking into account RACI’s position as a state-based organisation, capital adequacy requirements, and RACI’s ability to raise capital).
The competitive constraint from rival insurers on IAG post-Acquisition in Western Australia.
The likelihood, timeliness and sufficiency of new entry into or expansion of the supply of motor insurance in Western Australia, including the possible impediments to this.
The impact of the use of different brands (both underwriter and third-party brands) on competition for consumers.
How regulatory costs, claims cost volatility, reinsurance costs and geographic diversity impact RACI’s ability to supply motor vehicle insurance. Vertical effects
Whether there are regions in Western Australia where smash repair services are limited or capacity constrained.
The degree to which contractual arrangements with smash repairers provide for exclusivity or priority access.
The extent to which smash repairers in practice prioritise work from larger insurers.
The extent to which IAG would be in an enhanced position to foreclose or frustrate competing insurers' access to repairers post-Acquisition.
The likely effect of any foreclosure strategies, including the extent to which rival insurers would become less vigorous competitors in the supply of home and contents insurance and motor insurance.

phase2_notice_matters_to_investigate.heading: Competitive effects in the acquisition of motor vehicle smash repair services

The effect of lower repair prices on exit, entry, and investment decisions of smash repairers in Western Australia and/or certain regions in Western Australia.
